You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Light

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, light is the settled symbol of God's own nature and presence—His holiness, truth, and glory—and, derivatively, of Christ as the divine revelation and salvation given to the world. The core claim is twofold: God is light (utter purity and truth without any darkness), and Jesus Christ is 'the light of the world' who brings that divine life, truth, and salvation to humanity, dispelling the darkness of sin, ignorance, and death.",

    "1 John 1:5 ('God is light, and in him is no darkness at all')",
    "John 8:12 ('I am the light of the world')",
    "John 1:4-9 (the true light that gives light to everyone, coming into the world)",
    "Genesis 1:3 ('Let there be light'), often read typologically alongside 2 Corinthians 4:6",
    "2 Corinthians 4:6 (God who said 'let light shine out of darkness' has shone in our hearts)",
    "Psalm 27:1 ('The LORD is my light and my salvation')",
    "Isaiah 9:2 ('The people walking in darkness have seen a great light'), quoted in Matthew 4:16",
    "John 12:35-36, 46 (walk while you have the light; believe in the light)",
    "Revelation 21:23 (the Lamb is the lamp of the New Jerusalem)",
    "1 Timothy 6:16 (God dwells in unapproachable light)"
  ],
  "alternatives": [

        "Psalm 119:105 ('Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path')",
        "Psalm 119:130",
        "Proverbs 6:23",
        "2 Peter 1:19 (the prophetic word as a lamp shining in a dark place)"
      ],
      "prominence": "dominant"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Moral goodness and righteous living: light as holiness, purity, and ethical conduct opposed to the 'works of darkness'; believers are 'children of light' who must 'walk in the light.'",
      "basis": [
        "Ephesians 5:8-14 ('walk as children of light')",
        "1 John 1:6-7 (walking in the light vs. walking in darkness)",
        "Romans 13:12 ('put on the armor of light')",
        "1 Thessalonians 5:5"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "The church and believers as witnesses: Christians as reflected or derivative light bearing testimony to God in the world.",
      "basis": [
        "Matthew 5:14-16 ('You are the light of the world... let your light shine')",
        "Philippians 2:15 ('shine as lights in the world')",
        "Acts 13:47 (a light for the Gentiles, citing Isaiah 49:6)"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Salvation, deliverance, and eschatological blessing: light as the state of the redeemed, rescue from the 'domain of darkness,' and the glory of the age to come.",
      "basis": [
        "Colossians 1:12-13 (inheritance of the saints in light; delivered from the domain of darkness)",
        "1 Peter 2:9 ('called you out of darkness into his marvelous light')",
        "Isaiah 60:1-3, 19-20",

      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Eastern Orthodox 'uncreated light': the light of the Transfiguration understood (especially in Palamite/hesychast theology) as the uncreated divine energies, a real experiential participation in God rather than a mere metaphor.",
      "basis": [
        "Matthew 17:1-8 and parallels (the Transfiguration)",
        "Exodus 34:29-35 (Moses' shining face)",
        "2 Corinthians 3:18"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Life and joy/general well-being: a Hebrew-idiom reading in which light stands for life itself, prosperity, and favor (the 'light of life,' the 'light of the face').",
      "basis": [
        "Job 33:28, 30 ('the light of life')",
        "Psalm 4:6; Psalm 36:9 ('in your light we see light')",
        "Psalm 97:11",
        "John 8:12 ('light of life')"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Gnostic and esoteric readings: light as a divine spark or inner illumination within humans, part of a dualistic light-versus-darkness cosmology; historically influential but rejected by orthodox Christianity, though echoes appear in some mystical and Quaker ('Inner Light') traditions.",
      "basis": [
        "Appropriations of John 1 and Johannine light/darkness dualism in Gnostic texts",
        "Quaker appeal to John 1:9 (the light that enlightens every person)"
      ],
      "prominence": "rare"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "Light is one of the most stable and widely agreed symbols in Christian interpretation. The consensus is not a single narrow definition but a tightly related cluster: God's nature/presence, Christ as revealer and savior, divine truth, and derivative human holiness and witness. Commentators across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions treat these as facets of one symbol rather than competing readings. The listed 'alternatives' are mostly complementary emphases; only the Gnostic/esoteric reading is a materially different and historically contested interpretation. Any author claiming a novel or contrary primary meaning for 'light' would be departing from a very strong and well-documented consensus."
}

Matthew 5:16 — Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
